beats: [d:intrigue][sfx:boom][act:storytelling, drawing us in]In {1963|nineteen sixty-three}, in central ^Turkey, a man knocking through a wall in his ^basement found a ^room he never knew was there.
[d:tension][act:the reveal, low and slow]Below it: a whole ^city, ^eighty-five metres deep. [p:0.93][act:a sense of scale, hushed]About as deep as a twenty-five-storey building is ^tall.

[d:calm][act:touring it, fascinated]It's carved into soft volcanic rock called ^tuff: easy to cut, then it hardens in the ^air. [act:touring it, counting off]Up to ^eighteen floors, more than ^fifty air shafts, stables, wells and ^chapels.
[d:build][go:2|0][act:a clever detail, admiring]And each level could be sealed from ^inside, with a ^rolling stone door, like a giant millstone rolled across the ^passage.

[d:build][act:the real puzzle, curious][tune:fall]So how old is the ^deepest level? [act:presenting his idea, fairly]The writer Graham ^Hancock asks whether it began as a shelter from the ^Ice Age cold, twelve ^thousand years ago.

[d:build][sfx:shimmer][act:conceding, sincere]And he has a ^point: nobody has ever dated the ^digging itself. [p:0.93][act:explaining, an everyday picture]A carved room is like a hole in the ground: there's nothing in empty space to ^measure. [act:explaining, plain]You can only date what people left ^inside, or wrote ^down.

[d:build][act:naming the knowns, confident]And what we ^can date tells one story: chapels, stables, and written accounts of Arab ^raids from the {700s|seven hundreds} on. [act:plain, respectful]^Byzantine Christians, of the eastern Roman Empire, sheltered here.
[d:build][act:a quiet, human detail]Local Christians still used@verb it until {1923|nineteen twenty-three}, just forty years before that basement wall came ^down.
[d:reveal][act:widening the view, wonder]And it isn't ^alone: more than ^three hundred and sixty underground settlements have been located in ^Cappadocia, the region around it.

[d:build][go:6|0][sfx:hit][act:the catch, thoughtful]But carving ^erases its own history. [p:0.93][act:explaining, an everyday picture]Every time a room was enlarged, the older surface was scraped ^away, like a blackboard wiped clean and written on ^again.

[d:verdict][p:0.95][act:weighing the two options][tune:fall]Deepest levels from the ^Iron Age, nearly three thousand years ago, or the ^Ice Age? [act:the verdict, level-headed][tune:fall]*Awaiting ^evidence*. [act:the grounded option][tune:rise]A ^Byzantine refuge city? [act:plain and assured][tune:fall]That's what the evidence ^shows.
[d:tension][p:0.93][act:reflective, a little poetic]Soft rock keeps ^secrets. [act:the wry twist, light]It ^also keeps getting ^dug.
